execution_frontier.name: Perceptual CNS evaluation, Stage-D adaptation, and export
execution_frontier.summary: The direct exact-ID path has advanced through three real adaptation stages. Stage A completed 100 batches/200 optimizer steps on a balanced 128-row subset; Stage B completed 200 batches/400 optimizer steps on the full 799-row corpus; Stage C completed 100 targeted batches/200 optimizer steps for short-form and special-phone repair. Machine waveform acceptance advanced from 123/125 after Stage B to 125/125 after Stage C. Stage-C weights have been recovered and hash-verified in the current conversation. The remaining frontier is human/perceptual CNS evaluation, longer Stage-D adaptation from Stage-C weights, then export and final acoustic acceptance.

verified_achievements.fact: DWC language/etymology/PSS/CNS work progressed through the pre-audio TTS handoff.
An engine-independent DWC frontend exists that produces exact custom phoneme IDs.
A synthetic exact-ID aligned DWC bootstrap corpus of 799 utterances exists and passed exact-ID preflight.
The neural proxy rendered 199/199 DWC regression utterances with 0 unsupported CNS IPA symbols in that set and bypassed English G2P.
Piper v1.8.0 supports direct owner-supplied phoneme IDs and the warm-start mechanism used by the DWC path.
The pretrained Piper/LJSpeech checkpoint successfully warm-starts the DWC direct exact-custom-ID path without replacing the 58-symbol DWC embedding.
Stage A completed 100 training batches / 200 optimizer steps on a balanced 128-row subset.
Stage B completed 200 training batches / 400 optimizer steps on the full 799-row synthetic DWC corpus; machine waveform acceptance was 123/125.
Stage C completed 100 targeted batches / 200 optimizer steps for short-form/special-phone repair; machine waveform acceptance was 125/125.

Stage-C weights were reassembled in the 2026-09-08 recovery conversation: 281,775,417 bytes; SHA-256 d800ae031942c29289ced1cc80c1448fff234c53f42a56f2d69265e7e3ebabb2, matching the recorded recovery hash.

current_execution_surface.interpretation: Current sandbox can recover/inspect/package evidence but cannot serve as the sustained GPU Stage-D training surface. GPU absence is an execution-surface limitation only.

next_execution_sequence.action: Complete machine-side recovery and inspection of Stage-C evidence, identify the exact Stage-B review rows repaired by Stage C, and preserve verified hashes/configuration.

Prepare a structured human CNS perceptual evaluation gate using the Stage-B and Stage-C acceptance demos/manifests, emphasizing pronunciation fidelity, full-vowel preservation, stress/rhythm, difficult CNS phones, intelligibility, target accent/style, and meaning preservation.

Run longer Stage-D adaptation beginning from verified Stage-C weights, using the exact 58-ID DWC path and a curriculum that preserves the short-form/special-phone gains while extending full-corpus adaptation. Do not restart from LJSpeech warm-start or Stage A/B/C.
Produce a durable Stage-D checkpoint, hashes/config/training metrics, controlled evaluation renders, and rerun machine acoustic acceptance.
Select/export the candidate model and package its ONNX/config/phoneme map/provenance with explicit temporary-synthetic-voice status.
Replace the temporary synthetic acoustic target with human CNS recordings for the authentic production voice while preserving the settled exact-ID language architecture.

owner_or_environment_gates.perceptual_cns_evaluation: Requires human auditory judgment; machine waveform acceptance is not a substitute.
owner_or_environment_gates.stage_d_gpu: Requires a GPU-capable execution surface; the current sandbox reports no CUDA devices.

execution_rules.continue_semantics: Remain in execution mode until the largest safe bounded unit is verified complete or a genuine blocker is fully evidenced.
execution_rules.timeout_recovery: Resume at the failing boundary or take the defined execution-surface fallback; do not restart closed stages.
